201: Versailles of the Dead by Kumiko Suekane (Seven Seas) is a historical horror story that mixes the French court with the walking dead. When Marie Antoinette is killed on the road to France, her twin brother Albert takes her place and enters Versailles disguised as the future queen. He has to keep his secret while the dead begin to rise around him. It's a good pick for readers who like court intrigue, gender-bending disguise, and dark, gory twists on real history.
205: Rosen Blood by Kachiru Ishizue (Viz Media) is a gothic shojo romance with vampires. Stella, a young woman with nowhere left to go, collapses in the woods and wakes up in an old mansion. Its owner, the cold and handsome Levi, and the other residents turn out to be vampires. Stella decides to stay and work as a maid, and slowly learns their secrets. It's a lush, moody read for fans of romantic fantasy and pretty, detailed art.
208: Saber Marionette J by Satoru Akahori (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi comedy with plenty of heart. On the colony planet Terra II, where only men survived, women exist only as legends and robots called marionettes do the work. Otaru Mamiya, a kind young man with little money, accidentally awakens Lime, a cheerful marionette with a special circuit that lets her feel real emotions. Soon two more join her. It's a lighthearted, energetic series for fans of '90s anime comedy.
224: Scryed by Yosuke Kuroda (Tokyopop) is a hard-hitting action story about people with strange powers. After a disaster tears a region of Japan away from the rest of the country, some children born there develop abilities called Alters. Kazuma, a hot-headed young mercenary, uses his Alter to survive in the lawless Lost Ground. His path keeps crossing with Ryuho, a disciplined Alter user working for the government force HOLY. It's a fast read for fans of rival fights and gritty sci-fi.
225: WorldEnd by Akira Kareno (Yen Press) is a quiet, bittersweet fantasy set after the end of the world. Humans were wiped out long ago, and the survivors live on floating islands above a land overrun by monsters. Willem Kmetsch, the last human, wakes after five hundred years and takes a job as caretaker of a military warehouse. There he finds a group of young girls who fight with ancient weapons, including the gentle Chtholly. It's a tender, melancholy story for readers who like emotional fantasy.
227: Love Me for Who I Am by Kata Konayama (Seven Seas) is a warm, funny story about friendship and identity. Mogumo, a nonbinary high school student, has never felt like they fit in anywhere. Then a classmate invites them to work at a maid cafe staffed by boys dressed as girls. Mogumo isn't a boy, but the cafe turns into a place where they can finally be themselves. It's a gentle, thoughtful read for anyone who enjoys found-family stories with heart.
229: Love Roma by Minoru Toyoda (Del Rey) is a sweet, offbeat romantic comedy. Hoshino is an earnest high school boy who says exactly what he thinks. On the day he first meets his classmate Negishi, he tells her he likes her and asks her out. Negishi doesn't know what to make of him, but his honesty slowly wins her over. It's a charming, low-key story for readers who want a romance without the usual drama and misunderstandings.
233: Your Turn to Die by Nankidai (Yen Press) is a tense thriller based on the popular death-game visual novel. High school student Sara Chidouin wakes up trapped in a strange facility with a group of strangers and her close friend Joe. A mysterious host forces them into deadly games where they must vote on who lives. Trust is hard to come by, and everyone has something to hide. It's a gripping read for fans of mysteries, survival games, and stories full of twists.
234: Yozakura Quartet by Suzuhito Yasuda (Kodansha) is a supernatural action comedy set in a town where humans and yokai live side by side. Akina Hiizumi runs a small counseling office in the town of Sakurashin with his friends Hime, the teenage mayor, and Ao and Kotoha, who each have special powers. Together they help residents, settle disputes, and protect the town from threats. It's a lively, stylish series for fans of yokai stories with big personalities.
235: Guardian Angel Getten by Minene Sakurano (Tokyopop) is a magical comedy about a boy and his new guardian spirit. Tasuke Shichiri, a middle school student who lives on his own, receives a strange ring from his traveling father. When he looks through it, Shaorin, a guardian spirit sworn to protect him, appears in his room. She takes her duty very seriously, which causes plenty of trouble. It's a light, playful series for fans of classic magical-girlfriend comedies.
236: Eerie Queerie by Shuri Shimizu (Tokyopop) is a sweet and funny supernatural romance. Mitsuo is a shy, sensitive high school boy who can see ghosts, and they love to borrow his body. Many of the spirits have unfinished business, which usually means confessing their love to someone, and Mitsuo ends up making a scene at school. His classmates start to get the wrong idea. It's a cute, lighthearted read for fans of ghost stories and boys' love comedy.
241: Fangirl by Rainbow Rowell (Viz Media) is a manga adaptation of the beloved coming-of-age novel. Cath is starting college, and her twin sister Wren no longer wants to be her roommate. Shy and anxious, Cath would rather keep writing her popular fan fiction about the boy wizard Simon Snow than face new people. A grumpy roommate and a friendly classmate start to pull her out of her shell. It's a warm, relatable story for anyone who has loved a fandom.
243: Shaman King by Hiroyuki Takei (Kodansha) is a supernatural action series about spirits, friendship, and a tournament like no other. Manta Oyamada, a small and timid student, takes a shortcut through a graveyard and meets Yoh Asakura, a laid-back boy who can see and talk to ghosts. Yoh is a shaman, training to enter the Shaman Fight and become the Shaman King. It's a fun, big-hearted series for fans of classic shonen adventure.
248: Slayers by Hajime Kanzaka (Tokyopop) is a fantasy comedy light novel series that launched a classic anime. Lina Inverse is a teenage sorceress with a huge appetite, a quick temper, and very powerful magic. While on the road, she teams up with Gourry Gabriev, a kind but not very bright swordsman who thinks she needs protecting. Their adventure soon pulls them into a fight with dark forces. It's a fun, fast read for fans of sword-and-sorcery humor.
250: School Judgment by Nobuaki Enoki and Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a courtroom mystery with a playful twist. At Tenbin Elementary, disputes between students are settled in a classroom court. Abaku Inugami, a confident transfer student, is a skilled defense attorney who takes on a classmate accused of a crime he says he didn't commit. Each case is a puzzle of clues and arguments. It's a clever, quick read for fans of legal mysteries and sharp art.
260: Juni Taisen: Zodiac War by Nisio Isin (Viz Media) is a violent action thriller about a battle royale. Every twelve years, twelve warriors, each representing an animal of the Chinese zodiac, meet to fight to the death. The last one standing is granted any wish. Each fighter has their own skills, past, and reason for being there. It's a dark, fast-paced read for fans of survival battles with a large cast of strong characters.
261: Kagerou Daze by Jin (Yen Press) is a sci-fi mystery light novel series based on the popular Vocaloid songs. Shintaro Kisaragi is a shut-in who hasn't left his room in two years. When his computer breaks on a hot August day, he heads to a department store, which is suddenly taken over by armed attackers. He soon meets a group of young people with strange eye powers. It's a twisty read for fans of mysteries, time loops, and quirky casts.
262: The Angel Next Door Spoils Me Rotten by Saekisan (Square Enix) is a sweet, slow-burn romantic comedy. Amane Fujimiya is a high school student who lives alone and doesn't take good care of himself. One rainy day he lends his umbrella to Mahiru Shiina, the most admired girl at school, who happens to live next door. To repay him, she starts bringing him home-cooked meals. It's a cozy, gentle read for fans of everyday romance.
264: Higehiro by Shimesaba (Yen Press) is a heartfelt drama about two people who need each other's help. Yoshida is a 26-year-old office worker who has just been turned down by the coworker he likes. On his way home, he finds Sayu, a high school runaway, sitting by the road with nowhere to go. He lets her stay at his apartment, and an unusual living arrangement begins. It's a thoughtful, emotional read about growing up and healing.
265: Restaurant to Another World by Junpei Inuzuka (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy about food bringing people together. Western Restaurant Nekoya is a small diner in a Tokyo shopping district, closed every Saturday. On that day, its door opens into a fantasy world, and elves, warriors, dragons, and other unusual guests drop in for a meal. Each one finds a dish that becomes a favorite. It's a warm, comforting read for anyone who loves food stories.
267: Cross-Dressing Villainess Cecilia Sylvie by Hiroro Akizakura (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel with a romantic twist. Cecilia remembers her past life and realizes she has been reborn as the villainess of a dating game, destined to die. To avoid her fate, she disguises herself as a boy named Cecil and stays far away from the prince. Somehow, things don't go to plan. It's a fun, breezy read for fans of reincarnation and villainess stories.
270: Chaika: The Coffin Princess by Ichiro Sakaki (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure set after a long war. Toru Acura was trained as a saboteur, but now that peace has come, he has no purpose. Then he meets Chaika, a white-haired girl who carries a large coffin on her back and speaks in broken phrases. She wants to collect the remains of a fallen emperor, and Toru agrees to help. It's a fun, action-filled read for fans of quest stories.
271: Yokohama Kaidashi Kikou by Hitoshi Ashinano (Seven Seas) is a quiet, peaceful slice of life set after the world has slowly changed. Sea levels have risen and humanity is fading, but life goes on calmly. Alpha, a robot who looks like a young woman, runs a small coffee shop in the countryside while she waits for her owner to return. She meets neighbors, explores, and enjoys the moment. It's a gentle, beautiful read for anyone who wants something calm.
272: The Candidate for Goddess by Yukiru Sugisaki (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi action story about giant robots. In the far future, humanity's last planet is threatened by invaders called Victim. Zero Enna, a hopeful young boy, joins an academy that trains pilots for the Goddesses, the only machines that can fight back. He and his classmates must prove they can handle the pressure. It's a good pick for fans of mecha and academy stories.
276: Komomo Confiserie by Maki Minami (Viz Media) is a sweet romantic comedy about pastry and second chances. As a spoiled rich girl, Komomo Ichihara loved sweets and bossed around Natsu, a boy who lived at her family's estate. Years later, her family loses its fortune, and she ends up working at a pastry shop where Natsu is now a talented pastry chef. This time, he's the one in charge. It's a light, fun read for fans of shojo romance and food.
277: BL Metamorphosis by Kaori Tsurutani (Seven Seas) is a gentle, heartwarming story about an unlikely friendship. Ichinoi is a 75-year-old widow who stops in a bookstore and picks up a boys' love manga for its pretty cover. She's surprised to love it. Urara, the shy 17-year-old girl working at the counter, is a fan too, and the two start bonding over the series. It's a sweet, thoughtful read about loneliness, fandom, and finding your people.
278: Mushishi by Yuki Urushibara (Kodansha) is a quiet, atmospheric supernatural series. Mushi are simple, mysterious life forms that most people can't see, and they sometimes cause strange troubles for humans. Ginko, a white-haired mushi master, travels the countryside of old Japan to study them and help those who are affected. Each chapter is a mostly standalone tale. It's a calm, beautiful read for anyone who enjoys folklore and thoughtful stories.
279: Gate 7 by CLAMP (Dark Horse) is a fantasy action series set in modern-day Kyoto. Chikahito Takamoto, a high school student who loves Japanese history, finally gets to visit the ancient city. Almost right away, he stumbles into a hidden battle between people with strange powers and meets Hana, a mysterious girl at the center of it. It's a stylish read for fans of CLAMP's art, Japanese history, and supernatural fights.
282: Avatar: The Last Airbender by Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko (Tokyopop) is a kid-friendly adventure retold in manga form using art from the animated series. In a world where people can control the elements, the Fire Nation is at war with everyone else. Siblings Katara and Sokka find a boy frozen in an iceberg: Aang, the last airbender and the long-missing Avatar. It's a fun way for young fans to relive the show.
284: Zoids: Chaotic Century by Michiro Ueyama (Viz Media) is a kid-friendly action adventure about giant mechanical beasts. On planet Zi, metal creatures called Zoids are used in battle. Van Flyheight, a boy from a small desert village, finds a strange girl named Fiona and an organoid named Zeke in an old ruin. Soon he's riding into the middle of a war. It's a fun read for fans of robots, monsters, and big battles.
290: Act-Age by Tatsuya Matsuki (Viz Media) is a drama about acting and talent. Kei Yonagi is a high school girl who takes care of her younger siblings and dreams of becoming an actress. At an audition, her unusual method acting, where she fully becomes the role, catches the eye of an eccentric film director. He sets out to shape her into a star. It's an intense, inspiring read for fans of performing arts stories.
294: Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days by Shiro Amano (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure based on the popular video game. Roxas is the newest member of Organization XIII, a group of mysterious beings who have no memories of who they were. He's sent on missions to different worlds, and after work, he eats ice cream on a clock tower with his friends Axel and Xion. It's a warm, bittersweet read for fans of the games.
295: March Story by Hyung Min Kim (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy set in a gothic version of Europe. Evil spirits called ill hide inside beautiful antiques and possess the people who use them. March is a young girl who disguises herself as a boy and hunts ill as an Ill Hunter, carrying her own secret. Each case brings her face to face with greed and sorrow. It's a striking read for fans of moody, richly drawn fantasy.
